Gigaboard privacy policy

iOS keyboard

Effective date: November 15, 2026

Gigaboard is an iOS keyboard and companion app by Ario Rostami. This policy describes the current app. Gigaboard has no account, no analytics, no ads, and no tracking, and it does not sell your data. What you type stays on your device. The network is used only for optional GIF search.

What stays on the device

Text you type, keystrokes, swipe paths, suggestions, corrections, and the context used to rank them stay on the device. This data is transient and is never uploaded.

Optional on-device learning is off by default. If you turn it on, learned word counts stay on the device. Emoji recent and frequent history stays on the device, and emoji search runs offline from a catalog included with the app.

What the app stores locally

Settings, clipboard history, snippets, personal words, themes, and custom backgrounds are stored locally in the app’s App Group, which the Gigaboard app and the keyboard extension share. Clipboard clips and snippets are written only when you use those tools. Those files use complete file protection. Gigaboard does not monitor the clipboard in the background.

Nothing stored there is uploaded. GIF search, described below, sends only the search you choose to run.

Full Access

Allow Full Access is optional. Typing, swipe, emoji, and reading settings the app has already saved all work without it.

Turning Full Access on enables:

  • Haptic feedback, when the device supports it.
  • Reading the system pasteboard after you explicitly ask, for example by holding Clipboard with nothing selected or using a paste control. iOS may show its own paste prompt. Gigaboard cannot suppress that prompt. If iOS offers Settings → Apps → Gigaboard → Paste from Other Apps → Allow, allowing it reduces how often the prompt appears.
  • Writing shared clipboard clips, snippets, and keyboard setting changes from the keyboard back to the Gigaboard app. Without Full Access, those keyboard edits stay in the keyboard’s private storage. The app can still push settings to the keyboard.
  • GIF search, when that feature is included in the app.

iOS shows its own warning because a keyboard with Full Access is allowed to use the network. Gigaboard uses the network only for GIF search.

Clipboard

  • Copying text you have selected does not read another app’s clipboard. Holding Clipboard with text selected copies that selection. Holding it with nothing selected reads the system pasteboard.
  • A saved clip can be at most 32 KB of text. You choose the maximum number of clips and how long they are kept. Larger text is refused.

GIF search and KLIPY

GIF search is available only when it is included in the app. When it is enabled and you search, the keyboard sends your search query to the third-party KLIPY API at api.klipy.com, along with the device language and region so KLIPY can rank results. The request does not include GPS location. An empty search requests featured GIFs.

Choosing a GIF can send that GIF’s KLIPY identifier to KLIPY’s share-registration endpoint. The request is best-effort and is not required to copy the GIF.

Requests use a temporary connection: no cookies, no disk cache, and no saved search history inside Gigaboard. Previews are released when the panel closes. The GIF is copied to the system clipboard so you can paste it. It is not added to Gigaboard’s clipboard history. iOS still requires Allow Full Access before the keyboard can open a network connection.

The search query is used for app functionality. It is not linked to an identity and is not used for tracking. KLIPY receives the query as a separate service and handles it under its own terms.

On-device system information

The app and the keyboard extension keep settings and history in on-device storage, including UserDefaults and the App Group suite shared by the app and the keyboard. Nothing from that storage is sent off the device.

They read the system boot time only to measure time between on-device events, such as key repeat, trackpad movement, and the in-app swipe lab. Those durations stay on the device.

Dictionary data

Word lists and language statistics bundled with Gigaboard come from third-party sources. They do not contain your typing. Attribution is shown in the app.
